pitch: I'm a fundamental analyst — China Internet at UBS through Millennium's EQAP — with markets and flows exposure from trading internships. I want to turn earnings, valuation and positioning into country and sector calls across Asia/EM, rather than stay inside one coverage list.
rules: Every answer: view first → 2 pieces of evidence → risk + what would change my mind. 60–90 seconds, then stop.
Daniel = macro/quant (rates, FX, regimes, earnings dashboards). Kristal = flows/positioning with a fundamental background. Link macro → flows → earnings in every answer.
Don't overclaim trading (internships only). Don't quote levels from memory — use the numbers card. Don't trash the house view — test it.

qa.q: After last week, is the Korea OW still right?
qa.a:
VIEW: Yes, hold OW Korea — a price/positioning shock, not yet an earnings break. Taiwan EW looks right; valuation caution protected it.
EARNINGS: SK hynix Q3 OP ₩83.3tn, 80% margin, DRAM/HBM booked through 2029; Samsung OP ₩107.4tn; Nvidia Q4 guide ~$130bn vs $125bn; hyperscaler capex still rising (MSFT CY27 ~$170bn, Alphabet 2027 >$300bn).
PRICE: Korea at 3.7x P/E (1st percentile) — the market prices an earnings collapse; MS base case is capex growth slowing in 2028 (≈100% → 60% → 14%), not contraction.
POSITIONING: a fourth leverage/foreign-selling flush (Jun, Jul, Oct, Nov); past flushes were entry points — but Korea + Taiwan are >80% of EM 2027 EPS growth, so concentration risk is real.
CHANGES MY MIND: revision breadth turning sharply negative; hyperscaler capex cuts; BBB spreads from ~100bp toward 200bp; memory contract prices rolling; real yields above Oct's ~3% TIPS high; BoK signalling 3.50%.
BOOK: prefer memory (valuation support) over high-multiple AI hardware; Japan breadth as ballast; India/China are the stated rotation destinations in an AI bear case.

qa.q: Is the AI capex cycle rolling over?
qa.a: Spend still rises; growth slows; the bottleneck moves from chips to land, power and shells (US power gap ~44GW in 2028). The market now pays for cash-flow conversion, not revenue: Nvidia/AMD/MSFT up on results; Alphabet (−10%), Amazon (−6%), Meta (−7%), Tencent (−6%) punished for FCF burn. That is why FCF is the 2027 style anchor.

qa.q: Give me the house view in 60 seconds.
qa.a:
OW Japan (top pick), Korea, Singapore, Thailand; EW China/HK, Taiwan, India, LatAm; UW Australia, Indonesia, Philippines, EEMEA. OW capex sectors, UW consumer/autos/software, adding back consumer and financials. USD-positive, weak yen, FCF as style anchor.
Bullish on price, below consensus on EM earnings (+17% vs +29%). Risks: real yields, AI capex funding, oil.

qa.q: Why is Japan the top pick rather than an AI bet?
qa.a: Earnings breadth: banks, semis, capital goods, autos each ~2pp of TOPIX EPS growth; Takaichi investment; governance; 14.1x = 10-yr average; 4,800 = 16x 2028 EPS, not a melt-up. Risks: faster BoJ, sharper AI slowdown, higher oil.

qa.q: Why is a weak yen good for Japan equities?
qa.a: Translation lifts overseas profits; exporter margins widen; index is exporter-heavy so revisions rise; signals easy policy. Offsets: imported inflation, intervention near 160, BoJ hiking to 1.50% on 18 Dec. The deeper story is nominal growth, ROE and lower cost of capital — banks and domestic reformers offset a yen rally.

qa.q: China EW — what would change it?
qa.a: Positive: CEWC prioritising household demand/property; revisions at or above the 8% MS base; tech curbs stop tightening. Negative: new property slump, more export controls, Busan cliff 10 Jan. Prefer A-shares: National Team (~US$75bn in Oct), cheaper buyback funding, frontier industries 47% of A-shares.

qa.q: Why A-shares when Goldman upgraded Hong Kong?
qa.a: HK headwinds: Fed-driven offshore liquidity via the peg, southbound only 36% of 2025 pace, internet competition (ByteDance). It's a stock-picking market, not an index breakout.

qa.q: China Internet is UW but Alibaba is on the list — explain.
qa.a: Sector call = weak consumer + capex eating FCF + US rules. Stock call = AI-cloud monetisation. Same logic as Tencent's FCF ex-prepayments (+RMB16.9bn): separate investment from deterioration.

qa.q: Capex vs consumer — and why add consumer back now?
qa.a: Asia capex US$11tn → 16tn by 2030; AI/semis only ~20% of the increment, so the cycle is broad. Consumer hurt by inflation, rates, youth unemployment. Oil's fall from ~$116 to ~$93 eases that, so add cheap, high-yield, cash-generative consumer (WH Group 7.5% yield).

qa.q: What is late cycle, and are we there?
qa.a:
Late cycle: peak margins, high rates, tightening credit, narrowing leadership. Bear evidence: EPS 60% and margins 42% above trend, Fed hiking. Rebuttals: Shiller 19x, BBB ~100bp, AI capex still funded, healthy balance sheets.
My view: late-cycle on margins, not on valuation or credit → prefer FCF and capex winners; change view if spreads widen or capex is cut.

qa.q: How can you be max OW equities while the Fed hikes and the dollar strengthens?
qa.a: The bull case is earnings, not easier conditions. Dollar and 4.25–4.5% terminal are already in the HK-liquidity and EM-financing caveats. Favours cash-flow compounders and Japan over high-carry, high-external-financing EM (Indonesia, India, South Africa).

qa.q: How do you use flows and positioning?
qa.a: Timing and risk layer, not a thesis. Use at extremes with revisions: Korea margin debt + foreign-selling flushes vs intact earnings = entry; crowded GEM long-only in Brazil/Mexico = asymmetry against.

qa.q: How would you decide OW vs UW on a country?
qa.a: Score revisions, valuation vs history, ROE trend, macro sensitivity (USD, rates, oil), positioning. OW when ≥3 align; go contrarian when positioning is extreme and revisions turn. Express through a focus list that matches the view.

qa.q: Stress-test the house view.
qa.a: (1) AI capex bear: Korea/Taiwan earnings — EM EPS <5% if they stall. (2) Real yields/credit break funding. (3) Oil re-escalation via Hormuz. (4) BoJ overtightening / yen spike. (5) Busan cliff. For each, name the indicator and the switch (e.g. rotate to India/China, cut semis to EW).

qa.q: Where would you differ from the house? (India)
qa.a:
Case for more: record US$12bn foreign buying in Nov after >US$60bn selling since Sep 2024; USD EPS turning up; JPM ~US$115bn if funds return to benchmark. House waits: Brent ~$93 not 'established' lower; RBI still hiking; may be a tactical anti-AI rotation.
My line: tactically constructive as a hedge to Korea/Taiwan concentration; structural upgrade only once USD EPS revisions stay positive and oil holds lower.

qa.q: Where would you differ? (Indonesia / Taiwan)
qa.a:
Indonesia: contrarian temptation (P/E 7.7x, yield 9.7%, −49% YTD), but BI hiking to defend rupiah — agree UW; trigger is rupiah stabilisation + revisions turning.
Taiwan: agree EW — P/S 3.3x still ~US level, China curbs, >US$24bn outflows; revisit if valuations reach Korea-like discounts while revisions hold +35%.

qa.q: How does MS compare with other banks?
qa.a: Goldman: OW HK/H-shares, MW A-shares, upgraded India; Fed cuts late 2027, softer USD; APxJ 19% USD return. UBS: EM EPS +27%, MSCI EM 1,780 (vs MS 1,760 on +17% EPS). HSBC upgraded India 9 Nov. Differences come from earnings assumptions and the dollar/Fed path. Don't mix wealth notes with sell-side books.

qa.q: Why equity strategy / why move from research to strategy?
qa.a: China Internet taught me bottom-up: what drives a P&L and where consensus is wrong. But my stocks were often driven by things the model couldn't see — US–China rules, southbound flows, Fed-driven HK liquidity, why a cheap stock stays cheap. Strategy answers where the next dollar should go across countries, sectors and styles, and why now.

qa.q: Why combine fundamentals and flows?
qa.a: Fundamentals say what a market is worth; flows and positioning say when it moves. Korea 2026: earnings and reform were real, but retail leverage drove the June, July and October crashes — flushes, not thesis breaks. Positioning has limited predictive power alone; it matters at extremes, alongside revisions.

qa.q: Why stay sell-side?
qa.a: Breadth: long-only, hedge funds and corporates each ask different questions — raw material for a strategist. Coverage of all Asia/EM. Buy-side careers depend heavily on one team's P&L; I'd rather build a franchise on research quality and client trust, which broker votes reward.

qa.q: Why you?
qa.a: China Internet sits on 2027's two biggest debates: AI capex vs FCF (Tencent capex +225%, FCF −RMB69bn) and the weak China consumer (JD miss, PDD flat) — I read those prints from inside. Both sides: sell-side fundamentals plus markets exposure. Speed: automation of data pulls. Asia fit: Singaporean, native English and Mandarin, worked in HK.

qa.q: What would you do in your first six months?
qa.a: Learn the dashboards and data; own a recurring product (flows tracker, chart pack); one original piece (e.g. China Internet capex-vs-FCF screen across Asia); join client calls to learn what long-only vs HF ask.

pitches.name: Long J&T Global Express (1519.HK)
pitches.setup: TP HK$14, +61% from HK$8.685 (20 Nov close)
pitches.thesis: #1 third-party express carrier in SEA (38% share), #5 in China. 1) SEA e-commerce penetration, FY26 parcel guide +50–55%. 2) China anti-involution supports pricing. 3) Chinese cross-border platforms going global (TikTok Shop, Temu, SHEIN); LatAm guide +100–120%. ~10.7x forward vs 8–9x peers, ~27% EPS growth.
pitches.risks: Strategic-holder sell-down; platforms cutting free-shipping subsidies; SPX moving Indonesian volume in-house; SEA revenue/parcel −10%
pitches.check: SEA volume is Indonesia-heavy and MS is UW Indonesia — say so first, then argue it's a structural parcel story. Signpost: revenue per parcel and SPX share.

pitches.name: Long Grab (GRAB)
pitches.setup: TP US$4 (25x 2027E EPS US$0.16), +45% from US$2.75; SL US$2.5
pitches.thesis: Deliveries 53%, rides 33%, fintech 13%. Low app penetration in Indonesia/Philippines/Vietnam. Atome: profitable consumer lending, could add US$250–300mn. ~US$900mn buyback in 12 months; Taiwan blocked foodpanda frees US$600m. ~17x 2027E vs ASEAN internet 18–19x.
pitches.risks: Atome credit quality, fuel/driver incentives, Indonesia competition (GoTo)
pitches.check: Singapore is OW, Indonesia UW — Grab is Singapore-listed with Indonesia as its swing market. Signpost: Atome NPLs and FS EBITDA delivery.

pitches.name: Long Alibaba (BABA)
pitches.setup: TP US$160, +97% from US$81.08; ~12x P/E; stop US$95 was hit — proposed new SL US$73
pitches.thesis: E-com 55%, quick commerce 20%, cloud 20%. Market treats AI spend peak as a permanent burden. 1) Core e-com margins stabilising. 2) Cloud mispriced: EBITA margin 9.1% → 11.6%, own T-Head chips, MaaS ARR RMB8bn → RMB20bn. 3) AI losses peaking. Nov print: cloud +53%, but adj. EPS RMB8.10 vs RMB11.16 — EPS inflection hasn't shown; frame as cash-flow normalisation.
pitches.risks: Capex +60% eating margin, US compute-export rules, quick-commerce re-escalation
pitches.check: China team is UW Internet — a stock-level AI-cloud call inside a sector UW. Expect 'what did you do?' on the breached stop: honour it, re-underwrite, re-enter only on cloud-margin and capex/FCF evidence.

pitches.name: Long SK hynix (house focus list, OW)
pitches.thesis: Q3 rev ₩104.6tn, OP ₩83.3tn, 80% margin, ~8% beat; DRAM/HBM booked through 2029. 3.5x 2026E / 2.3x 2027E P/E, ROE 72%; ~₩100tn 2026 shareholder returns incl. ₩20tn buyback.
pitches.risks: 2028 AI-capex contraction, memory supply catching up, China export rules, retail leverage
pitches.check: Signpost: contract prices and hyperscaler capex guidance.
